neet_phy_u14_t09_1.working: A transformer works by mutual induction from a changing flux, so the secondary EMF has the same frequency as the primary. Voltage, current and number of turns all change in a step-up transformer.

neet_phy_u14_t09_2.working: Output power = 11 × 4 = 44 W. Input power = 44 / 0.8 = 55 W. Primary current Ip = 55 / 220 = 0.25 A.

neet_phy_u14_t09_3.working: At 20 kV the line current is I = 100 kW / 20 kV = 5 A. Loss = I²R = 25 × 5 = 125 W. Check: at 10 kV, I = 10 A and loss = 500 W, so doubling the voltage cuts the loss by a factor of 4.

neet_phy_u14_t09_4.working: Flux leakage is reduced by winding the coils one over the other (A-IV). Copper loss is reduced by thick wires (B-II). Eddy-current loss is reduced by a laminated core (C-I). Hysteresis loss is reduced by a soft-iron core with a narrow loop (D-III).

neet_phy_u14_t09_5.working: A is true: voltage rises and current falls. B is false: steady DC gives no changing flux, so no induced EMF. C is true: frequency is unchanged. D is false: an ideal transformer conserves power. E is true: lower line current reduces I²R losses. Correct set is A, C and E.
